chapter: Orrin Blackstone and the record shop
title: Meeting Orrin, reading Down Beat and Esquire
summary: Allen met Blackstone in 1945 and read Down Beat; Steinau read Esquire, which he feels slowed his interest in jazz.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: mm-hmm well I thought that gee I guess I met Orrin in 1945 he just opened up the shop and it would have been probably in the summer I'd have to think about my navy days and when I went in and because I was extremely young I would have been 18 years old like 18 yeah 18 years old and uh yeah our birthdays are within a month of each other so so we're about to now I ought to yeah anyway but anyway uh and somehow I had been reading down downbeat and had gotten very uh that's something we haven't mentioned at all what's down the magazines that were around

I'd never heard of downbeat except I don't think I'd ever heard of downbeat at all I know that in the early 40s I would read Esquire yeah which somehow or other I took to be the the arbeiter of of taste for men anyway mm-hmm and besides of course being interested in looking at the petty girl pictures I don't remember whether they had a centerfold or whether it was or quite what it was that was where the petty girls were and I'd read their articles in fact I'd read the whole damn magazine which I always did at that time anyway and I'd read their articles on on food and drink and jazz and their short stories on jazz and they always sounded really great and almost orgasmic in all of these areas which I found pretty disappointing when I started drinking and I'm not sure that the gourmet food was much better but the jazz that they were talking about or the jazz musicians who basically were swing musicians for the most part didn't really greatly appeal to me when I heard some of the things so I suspect maybe in a sense uh that may have slowed me down in getting interested in jazz rather than
